Bottleneck: at small n (shapes 0,1,2: n=32/176/352, batch 20/40/40) cuSOLVER per-launch overhead dominates (~16us per 32x32 QR). Write a custom load_inline CUDA kernel: one threadblock factors one matrix entirely in shared memory via classic Householder QR, producing H/tau directly, batched across all matrices in a single launch. n=176 (124KB) fits B200 smem; column-tile n=352. Eliminate the launch storm.

Custom smem Householder QR for n<=200 (one block/matrix, right-looking unblocked, smem column-major). shape0 315.6->73.8us (4.3x), shape1 20024->2051us (9.8x). Geomean 44709.995->26188.222 (1.71x). Kernel is 53% of GPU time at 4.4ms/launch for n=176; trailing-update inner loop is O(n^2) serial per thread -> needs parallel rank-1 update.
Block-parallel trailing update (warp-per-column dots + flat 2D rank-1 update), 256 threads. shape0 73.8->41.0us, shape1 2051->1001us (20x vs baseline). Geomean 21714.845 (2.06x).

Blocked panel-in-smem QR for n in (234,512]; covers shapes 2,3. Panel PB=32 cols factored in smem, reflectors applied to trailing global submatrix sequentially. shape2 (n=352) 51102->47493us (1.08x), shape3 (n=512,b=640) 1071052->441952us (2.42x). Geomean 18936.107 (2.36x). Trailing update global-mem bound (no GEMM reuse) -> next WY+GEMM.

WY/T-factor GEMM trailing update for blocked kernel: A2-=V T(V^T A2), larft T built in smem + tiled GEMMs. FAILS validation, factor residual ~6500 vs allowed (WY math bug in trailing update). Full-smem path (n<=234) unaffected.

Fix WY trailing update to use T^T (geqrf applies Q_block^T=I-V T^T V^T). WY/GEMM block reflector now correct. shape2 (n=352) 47493->10795us (4.78x vs base), shape3 (n=512,b=640) 441952->142692us (7.5x vs base). Geomean 13043.450 (3.43x). GEMMs still naive FP32 (strided global reads) -> next: tensor cores / better memory access.

Coalesced warp-tiled WY GEMM (warp owns 32 consecutive trailing cols, reduction over rows outer). Validates. Geomean 13150 (neutral vs iter5 13043). Coalescing global A2 access did NOT help -> kernel is latency/occupancy bound, not bandwidth bound. shape2 11164, shape3 146300. Sets up tensor-core trailing GEMM.

In-smem blocked WY kernel for 48<n<=205: REGRESSION. n=176 1001->3764us (3.7x WORSE). WY/larft/tiling overhead dominates when trailing work small; unblocked full-smem wins for small n. Geomean 15889 (worse than iter6 13150). Reverting dispatch next: unblocked full-smem for n<=234, global blocked above. Crossover for blocking is >176.
Revert dispatch: unblocked full-smem for n<=236, global blocked WY above. Restores best on-brief result. shape0 41, shape1 1001, shape2 11164, shape3 146319us. Geomean 13151.658 (3.40x vs baseline).

Cooperative multi-block WY QR (grid=(NB,B), grid.sync) for under-occupied large-n shapes: NB blocks/matrix use idle SMs. Slice 0 factors panel+T(global scratch); all slices update disjoint trailing chunks. Single cooperative launch. shape2 (n=352,b=40) 11164->7536us (1.48x better, 6.85x vs base). High-batch (n=512,b=640) keeps 1-block path. Geomean 12429.596 (3.60x). Validates all 19.

Coop kernel: every slice self-factors panel+builds T in own smem (no idle slices, no global T scratch/reload, 1 grid.sync/panel). shape2 7536->7382us. Geomean 12395.554 (3.61x). Coop kernel now 23.7% occupancy (was 12.5% one-block); still smem-limited to 25% theoretical.

Refactor dispatch: cooperative for under-occupied n>=256, full-smem unblocked for small/well-occupied, single-block blocked for high-batch large-n. No benchmark change (12396.461, same kernels per shape). Clean foundation; n=512 test shapes now validated through coop path.

Experiment: lowered coop eligibility to n>=128 to route n=176 through cooperative blocked kernel. Result: n=176 1001->2065us WORSE (geomean 13746), confirming crossover is between 176 and 352 (WY/blocking overhead beats occupancy gain at n=176, matches in-smem-blocked finding). Reverted threshold to n>=256; resting state unchanged at 12396.461 (iter11 commit). No net code change.

Brief 0 DONE. Best: commit b96afdf, geomean 12396.461us = 3.61x vs baseline (44709.995). Brief fulfilled+exceeded. WHAT WORKED: (1) custom single-launch smem Householder QR, one block/matrix -> killed cuSOLVER launch storm: shape0 n=32 315->41us (7.7x), shape1 n=176 20024->1001us (20x); (2) block-parallel warp-per-column trailing update; (3) BLOCKED WY QR with larft T-factor + tiled GEMM trailing update (matrix in global, panel in smem) for n>234: shape2 n=352 51607->7382us (7.0x), bonus shape3 n=512/b640 1075104->146335us (7.3x); KEY FIX: trailing update must use T^T (geqrf applies Q^T=I-V T^T V^T), not T; (4) COOPERATIVE multi-block kernel (grid=(NB,B), grid.sync) for under-occupied shapes (B<#SMs, n>=256): each slice self-factors panel, all slices update disjoint trailing chunks -> shape2 occupancy 12.5%->23.7%, 11164->7382us. WHAT DIDN'T: blocking/coop REGRESS n<=176 (WY/larft overhead beats occupancy gain; full-smem unblocked wins for small n -- crossover is between 176 and 352); pure TF32 would fail stress-case validation. CURRENT LIMITS: coop kernel smem-bound to 25% theoretical occupancy; compute only ~10% (barrier-stall bound). NEXT-BRIEF IDEAS: (A) TENSOR CORES for trailing GEMM via 3xTF32/split-float (FP32 accuracy, ~2.6x on GEMM) -- biggest lever for shapes 2,3, but complex rewrite; (B) extend custom kernel to n>=1024 shapes 4,5,6 (currently torch.geqrf fallback, 242/77/54ms -- OFF my brief but big absolute geomean opportunity, same launch-storm pattern); (C) reduce coop smem to lift occupancy past 25%. ACCEPTED designs: (1) pure torch, or (2) ALL compute inside NULL-default-stream custom kernels launched as <<<grid,block,smem>>> with NO stream arg, using torch only for allocation and for torch.geqrf on shapes that touch no custom kernel. Your current best accepted submission is W1-style 13244us (3.37x); the locally-faster recursive+torch.bmm hybrids are leaderboard-DEAD. Your b96afdfa submission is the current VALID champion (3.61x local, accepted on leaderboard) — monolithic NULL-stream kernel for n<=512, torch.geqrf for n>512. Extend the custom blocked-WY kernel to cover n=1024/2048 (shapes 4,5) so they stop falling back to geqrf, keeping the trailing update as a NULL-stream-0 CUDA GEMM kernel (NOT torch.bmm). Profile shape 4 first. Keep all 19 validating; emit native H/tau. This is pure valid upside on a known-accepted design.

Route n=2048 (shape 5) through PB=16 coop kernel: REGRESSION. shape5 76993(geqrf)->252758us (3.3x WORSE). Validates (dense+rankdef stress pass, residuals in tol). Root cause: coop design has EVERY slice self-factor the full panel redundantly (NB=16 slices each factor 2048x16 panel, x128 panels) - redundancy explodes at n=2048. PB=16 also halves GEMM intensity + 128 grid.syncs. Need: dedicated large-n design (single block per matrix is also bad at batch=8 occupancy=5%; need cooperative WITHOUT redundant panel factor, or tensor-core GEMM). geomean 10976->13003 (worse). Keeping iter1 (n=1024 coop) as best so far.

Route n=1024 (shape 4) through coop WY kernel (raise _CUSTOM_MAX_N 512->1024). shape4 241850(geqrf)->103141us (2.34x). Validates all 19. geomean 12396->10976 (4.07x vs baseline). ncu: coop kernel smem-bound to 1 block/SM (192KB), 12.5% occupancy, 0.81 waves (NB=2,B=60->120 blocks on 148 SMs), compute 16.9% DRAM 0.5% - occupancy-starved, latency-bound. COMMIT 07bfc191.

Lead-factor coop (slice 0 factors, sync, all slices update from global) for n>=768: REGRESSION. shape4 (n=1024) 103141->135081 (+31%: idle slices during serial panel factor + 2nd grid.sync/panel hurt); shape5 (n=2048,PB=16) 252758->365319 (WORSE than per-slice: idle-during-factor cost EXCEEDS redundant-factor saved). KEY FINDING: at large n the column-by-column Householder PANEL FACTOR is a serial bottleneck (tall 2048-row panel); neither redundant(per-slice) nor lead(idle) helps - this is why cuSOLVER geqr2_smem_domino + panel look-ahead wins. geomean 14247 (worse). Validates all 19. Reverting to iter1 (n=1024 per-slice coop + n=2048 geqrf = 10976). Next: V-from-global tiled GEMM to lift shape4 occupancy past 12.5% (drop 128KB Vp from smem).

SEPARATE-LAUNCH blocked WY (the brief's 'trailing update as NULL-stream GEMM kernel' design): host loops panels on NULL stream launching (1) panel_factor_kernel [1 block/matrix, smem-heavy, small work] + (2) trailing_wy_kernel [grid over trailing-cols x batch, V read from global row-tiled into smem, HIGH occupancy]. Decouples smem-heavy factor (occupancy-capped) from compute-heavy GEMM (occupancy-rich). shape4 (n=1024) 103141->24362us = 9.9x vs baseline (was 2.34x via fused coop, occupancy 12.5%->now high). KEY BUGS FIXED: (a) divergent __syncthreads when warp owns no cols -> set TWT=THREADS so each thread owns exactly 1 trailing column; (b) Vtile padding cols c>=pw uninitialized -> NaN -> stage all PB cols with 0-pad. shape5 (n=2048,PB=16) 108514 still loses to geqrf 76993. Validates all 19. geomean 10976->9378 = 4.77x vs baseline. NEW BEST. COMMIT c28a120.

Route n=2048 back to torch.geqrf (_CUSTOM_MAX_N=1536). Profiling showed n=2048 separate-launch trailing_wy_kernel is 88.9% of time (PB=16 hand-GEMM) and loses to geqrf's CUTLASS SIMT sgemm: 108514 vs 76993us. So geqrf is the leaderboard-correct choice for n=2048 until a faster (tensor-core) trailing GEMM lands. s5 76993 (1.0x). n=1024 separate-launch retained (24381us, 9.9x). geomean 9378->8932 = 5.01x vs baseline. NEW BEST. COMMIT bb0c204. NOTE: shape4 trailing GEMM is 78% of its time, shape3 (146ms, n=512) also hand-GEMM -> tensor cores is the next big lever for both.

MAJOR WIN: route ALL n>=256 (shapes 2,3,4) through separate-launch blocked GEMM (lowered threshold from n>=768). shape2 (n=352) 7382->2749 (2.7x), shape3 (n=512,batch640) 146336->26518 (5.5x, this was the LARGEST absolute time!), shape4 (n=1024) 24360 unchanged. The high-occupancy trailing_wy_kernel (V from global, row-tiled, tiny smem) beats BOTH the old coop kernel (n=352) AND the single-block blocked kernel (n=512,b640) - the single-block did trailing GEMM in 1 block/matrix; separate-launch spreads it across ntiles*B blocks for far better SM utilization. Validates all 19. geomean 8932->6075 = 7.36x vs baseline. NEW BEST. COMMIT 341c138. NOTE THIS IS A NEW VALIDATED BEST FOR THE MANAGER TO SUBMIT.

Trailing GEMM occupancy boost: keep W=V^T A2 and Y=T^T W ENTIRELY in per-thread registers (wcol[PB], one column/thread), eliminating the 2*PB*TWT=64KB W/Y smem that capped occupancy at 2 blocks/SM (25%). Now smem=Vtile+Tsm=~12KB. Phase B (T^T W) becomes a per-thread upper-tri mat-vec in registers (T from smem). ncu had shown trailing kernel L1/TEX 63.5%, occupancy 25% smem-bound. shape3 (n=512,b640) 26518->18780 (1.41x), shape2 2506, shape4 22151. Validates all 19. geomean 6075->5628 = 7.94x vs baseline. NEW BEST. COMMIT d589eed.

Trailing GEMM tuning: (1) generalized to CT trailing-cols/thread; tested CT=2 register tiling - REGRESSED to 6460 (wcol[CT][PB] register pressure dropped occupancy more than it cut L1 traffic), so CT=1 (W fully in regs) is best. (2) RB row-tile 64->256: fewer __syncthreads staging passes, shape3 18780->18388, shape4 22151->21397. ncu(shape3 trailing): occupancy 25%->37.5% after W-in-regs, now register-limited (72regs, 3blk/SM), compute 61% L1/TEX 73.7% - balanced. geomean 5628->5574 = 8.02x. Validates 19. COMMIT c5472b3. NEW BEST. Remaining levers: tensor cores on trailing GEMM (would help s3/s4 and maybe beat geqrf at s5).

Knob sweeps + refactor (no net perf change, same 5573 as c5472b3). Findings: (a) decoupled factor-threads/trailing-threads; TT=512 trailing REGRESSED to 5949 (wcol[32] reg pressure cuts occupancy, coarser TWT=512 hurts batch-640 load balance); (b) n=2048 PB=24 (max that fits 192KB factor smem; PB=28 exceeds 227KB smem cap -> invalid arg) gives 79530us, IMPROVED from PB=16's 108135 but STILL loses geqrf 76886 -> n=2048 stays geqrf.
